newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain blasts Cuba for blackballing its ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Spain blasts Cuba for blackballing its ambassador.

text.p: Spain's conservative government reacted angrily on Tuesday to the reported withdrawal by Cuba of the credentials of its ambassador to Havana.
"It's a big mistake, in a word," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes, who has spearheaded Madrid's new hard line against Cuban leader Fidel Castro, told state radio.
He said Madrid had yet to receive formal confirmation of the Cuban move against its ambassador which according to local media was announced in Tuesday's issue of the official newspaper Granma.

The Cuban government's reported move caps weeks of growing tension between Havana and Madrid, where conservative Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar has broken with the friendly approach towards Castro favoured by his predecessor Felipe Gonzalez during 13 years of Socialist rule.
At Aznar's behest, Spain is trying to push its 14 European Union partners into a harder line against Castro that would mesh in with Washington's efforts to push for democracy in Cuba.
Without naming him, Castro blasted Aznar in a speech this week, accusing him of taking money from what he described as a mafia of Cuban exiles in Miami.
